ra: Woden is the chief deity of the reconstructed Anglo-Saxon pantheon (Pollington).
Thunor is a core Anglo-Saxon god attested in place-names and the weekday.
Tiw is a core Anglo-Saxon god attested in place-names and the weekday.
Frige is the principal Anglo-Saxon goddess, attested in the weekday Friday.
Eostre is attested by Bede as an Anglo-Saxon goddess (month Eosturmonath).
Hreda is attested by Bede as an Anglo-Saxon goddess (month Hredmonath).
Seaxneat heads the East Saxon royal genealogy as a divine ancestor.
Ing is named in the Old English Rune Poem as an Anglo-Saxon deity.
Wuldor is a glory-god inferred for the Anglo-Saxon pantheon from lexis and place-names.
Erce is the earth-mother invoked in the Anglo-Saxon Aecerbot charm.
Woden is the Old English reflex of the same Germanic deity as Norse Odin (Wodanaz).
Thunor is the Old English cognate of Norse Thor (Thunraz).
Tiw is the Old English cognate of Norse Tyr (Tiwaz).
Frige is the Old English cognate of Norse Frigg (Frijjo).
Ing/Ingui corresponds to Norse Yngvi-Freyr, the Ingaevonic ancestor-deity.
Wuldor is the Old English lexical and divine cognate of Norse Ullr.
Erce the Old English earth-mother is functionally aligned with the Germanic earth-goddess Nerthus described by Tacitus.
